title: Postmortem: Kernel selection & scheduler change caused 2026-03-09 inference regression
creator: Alex Chen
description: Postmortem and follow-up action items for the Mar 9 2026 inference regression affecting hosted API and Dedicated customers. Regression manifested as elevated P95/P99 latency and GPU utilization after a scheduler change and kernel selection fallback introduced in runtime-1.20. This ticket tracks root cause, mitigations, and owners for permanent fixes.
incident_summary: On 2026-03-09 at ~03:14 UTC we observed a sustained increase in inference latency and token cost for text-generation workloads on the hosted fleet. The issue affected models using FlashAttention kernels and dynamic KV cache eviction patterns. Initial mitigation reduced customer impact; this ticket documents the postmortem and action items to prevent recurrence.
timeline:
2026-03-09 03:10 UTC - Alert: p99 latency spike on region-us-west hosting tier.
2026-03-09 03:14 UTC - Pager dispatched to on-call infra and runtime engineers.
2026-03-09 03:25 UTC - Rollback of scheduler change (PR #4210) on a subset of hosts; partial improvement observed.
2026-03-09 04:00 UTC - Full rollback completed; p99 latency returned close to baseline over 30m.
2026-03-09 05:30 UTC - Post-incident triage started; kernel selection component logs collected and traced.
2026-03-10 11:00 UTC - Root cause hypothesis confirmed: aggressive scheduler patch caused kernel selection to fall back to generic kernels and increased KV cache churn.
root_cause: A scheduler adjustment (PR #4210) intended to reduce tail latency introduced micro-scheduling jitter that changed request batching patterns. Under the new scheduler, certain sequence-length distributions triggered the kernel selector to prefer a conservative generic GEMM kernel path instead of optimized FlashAttention kernels because of altered memory alignment and batch composition heuristics. Additionally, a bug in the KV cache retention heuristic caused premature eviction under the new scheduling cadence, increasing cache misses and recomputation. The combination led to ~2x latency for affected sequences and higher GPU SM utilization.
impact_metrics:
Affected clusters: hosted-us-west and a subset of Dedicated pools.
P95 latency baseline: 230ms -> incident peak: 430ms (+87%).
P99 latency baseline: 480ms -> incident peak: 980ms (+104%).
Token cost: +18% for affected workloads during window.
Customer tickets opened: 12 active SRE/CS escalations.
Uptime SLA impact: minor (short windows) but measurable latency SLO violations for some customers.
mitigation_taken:
Immediate actions:
- Rolled back scheduler change (PR #4210) within 40 minutes.
- Reverted kernel selector to last-known-good heuristics (hotfix PR #4216) on critical pools.
- Increased KV cache grace period to reduce premature eviction.
Monitoring/alerts:
- Added temporary alert for kernel-selection fallback rate > 0.5% (alert ID INF-KS-3).
- Instrumented additional metrics for batch composition, kernel choice, and cache hit rate.
action_items: ENG-6730: Add deterministic unit and e2e tests for kernel selector under varied batch shapes (owner: Sara Li, due: 2026-03-24)
ENG-6731: Rework scheduler heuristics to preserve batching stability; include simulation harness before rollout (owner: Priya Patel, due: 2026-04-04)
ENG-6732: Fix KV cache heuristic bug and add regression tests for eviction logic (owner: Jordan Kim, due: 2026-03-28)
ENG-6733: Implement graceful fallback that prefers optimized kernels given minimal memory misalignment (owner: Mateo Ruiz, due: 2026-04-01)
ENG-6734: Add canary rollout + automated rollback for scheduler/kernel-selector changes in runtime deploy pipeline (owner: DevOps Team, due: 2026-04-08)
ENG-6735: Post-release performance benchmark suite in CI with p95/p99 regression gating for key models (owner: Research/Applied ML, due: 2026-04-15)
notes:
Trade-offs discussed: tighter scheduler constraints reduce batching variability but may increase queueing latency in rare cases. Decided to prioritize deterministic batching and kernel choice stability to protect tail latency.
PR review feedback: require microbenchmark graphs per commit that touch scheduler or kernel selector.
Customer communication: status updates sent via status.redwood.ai and targeted emails to affected accounts.
